metadata.hierarchy_description: The document organizes actionable requirements under main domains, subdomains, main controls, and sub-controls. The coding scheme identifies the domain, subdomain, main control, and sub-control.

requirements.source_reference: DCC Scope of Work and DCC Statement of Applicability
requirements.source_text: Every organization within the scope of these controls must comply with all applicable controls in this document.
requirements.source_summary: Organizations within the scope of the controls must comply with all controls that apply to them.

todo.name: Determine and document applicable DCC controls
todo.description: Assess the organization’s scope and data classification context, identify all applicable DCC controls, and record the applicability decisions for implementation and monitoring.

policies.name: DCC Compliance Policy
policies.description: Define the organization’s commitment and governance approach for complying with applicable Data Cybersecurity Controls.

policies.name: Control Applicability and Exception Policy
policies.description: Establish how control applicability, exclusions, and approved exceptions are assessed, documented, and maintained.

documents.name: DCC Statement of Applicability
documents.description: Record the controls determined to be applicable, including the basis for each applicability decision.

documents.name: DCC Compliance Plan
documents.description: Track implementation activities, responsible owners, status, and remediation for applicable controls.

evidence.name: Approved Statement of Applicability
evidence.description: Current approved record showing the applicable controls and supporting rationale.

evidence.name: Control implementation status reports
evidence.description: Reports or tracking records demonstrating that applicable controls are implemented or being remediated.

requirements.source_text: all organizations within the scope of these controls must implement whatever necessary to ensure continuous compliance with the controls
requirements.source_summary: Organizations within the scope of the controls must implement whatever is necessary to ensure continuous compliance with the controls.

todo.name: Establish continuous DCC compliance monitoring
todo.description: Implement governance, monitoring, and remediation processes that identify and address changes or deficiencies affecting ongoing compliance with applicable DCC controls.

policies.name: Continuous Compliance Monitoring Policy
policies.description: Define responsibilities and methods for monitoring compliance with applicable DCC controls over time.

policies.name: Cybersecurity Issue and Remediation Policy
policies.description: Set out how compliance gaps are recorded, assigned, tracked, and resolved.

documents.name: DCC Compliance Monitoring Plan
documents.description: Describe the monitoring activities, control owners, review inputs, and escalation arrangements used to support continuous compliance.

documents.name: Compliance Issues and Remediation Register
documents.description: Record identified deficiencies, corrective actions, owners, status, and closure information.

evidence.name: Compliance monitoring records
evidence.description: Completed monitoring checklists, dashboards, or review reports showing ongoing assessment of applicable controls.

evidence.name: Remediation records
evidence.description: Issue tickets, action plans, and closure evidence demonstrating that identified compliance gaps are addressed.

requirements.source_text: 1-1-1With reference to ECC control 1-8-1, the cybersecurity function in the organization must review the implementation of the Data Cybersecurity Controls periodically as specified for each data classification level.At least annually
requirements.source_summary: The organization’s cybersecurity function must periodically review implementation of the DCC, with the required review period determined by data classification and including at least an annual review requirement.

todo.name: Conduct and record cybersecurity function DCC reviews
todo.description: Schedule and perform reviews by the cybersecurity function at the applicable data-classification interval, ensuring the required annual review is completed and findings are tracked.

policies.name: Cybersecurity Control Review Policy
policies.description: Define the cybersecurity function’s responsibility, review scope, classification-based frequency, and follow-up process for DCC implementation reviews.

documents.name: DCC Review Schedule
documents.description: List applicable data classifications, required review intervals, assigned reviewers, and planned completion dates.

documents.name: DCC Implementation Review Report
documents.description: Document review procedures, results, identified gaps, and corrective actions.

evidence.name: Completed cybersecurity review reports
evidence.description: Signed or approved reports showing that the cybersecurity function reviewed DCC implementation.

evidence.name: Review schedule and action tracking
evidence.description: Records demonstrating review timing and follow-up of identified findings.

requirements.source_text: 1-1-2With reference to ECC control 1-8-2, cybersecurity review and audit must be conducted periodically by independent parties outside the organization’s cybersecurity function as specified for each data classification level.At least every 2yearsAt least annually
requirements.source_summary: Cybersecurity reviews and audits must be conducted periodically by independent parties outside the organization’s cybersecurity function, at intervals determined by data classification; the source specifies intervals of at least every two years and at least annually for the applicable classifications.

todo.name: Schedule independent DCC reviews and audits
todo.description: Arrange reviews or audits by qualified parties outside the cybersecurity function according to the applicable data-classification interval, and track resulting findings to closure.

policies.name: Independent Cybersecurity Audit Policy
policies.description: Define independence expectations, qualification criteria, classification-based audit frequency, scope, reporting, and follow-up.

documents.name: Independent Audit Program
documents.description: Document the audit schedule, scope, criteria, assigned independent party, and reporting arrangements.

documents.name: Audit Findings and Corrective Action Register
documents.description: Track findings, responsible owners, target actions, and closure evidence from independent reviews.

evidence.name: Independent audit reports
evidence.description: Reports issued by parties outside the organization’s cybersecurity function, including scope, results, and findings.

evidence.name: Auditor independence and engagement records
evidence.description: Engagement documentation showing the auditor’s organizational independence and assigned work.

evidence.name: Corrective action closure records
evidence.description: Evidence that findings from independent reviews were addressed and validated.

requirements.source_text: 2-1-1-1Strict restriction toallow only the minimum number of personnel accessing, viewingand sharingdata based on lists of privileges limited to Saudi-national employees unless exempted bythe Authorizing Official(the head of the organization or his/her delegate) and those lists are approved by the Authorizing Official.
requirements.source_summary: Access, viewing, and sharing of data must be strictly limited to the minimum number of personnel, using approved privilege lists limited to Saudi-national employees unless the Authorizing Official grants an exemption. The privilege lists must be approved by the Authorizing Official.

todo.name: Restrict and approve data access privileges
todo.description: Review personnel access needs, limit access, viewing, and sharing to the minimum necessary, maintain privilege lists reflecting the stated personnel restriction, and obtain Authorizing Official approval for the lists and any exemptions.

policies.name: Data Access Control Policy
policies.description: Define least-privilege access, viewing, and sharing requirements for data and the approval responsibilities of the Authorizing Official.

policies.name: Access Exception Policy
policies.description: Define how exemptions to the stated personnel restriction are requested, justified, approved, reviewed, and withdrawn.

documents.name: Approved Data Privilege Lists
documents.description: Maintain current lists of personnel authorized to access, view, or share data, including applicable approvals and exemptions.

documents.name: Access Exception Register
documents.description: Record Authorizing Official approvals for permitted exemptions, their scope, justification, and status.

evidence.name: Authorizing Official approvals
evidence.description: Approved privilege lists and documented approvals for applicable exemptions.

evidence.name: Access rights reports
evidence.description: System-generated reports showing personnel with data access, viewing, or sharing permissions.

evidence.name: Access review records
evidence.description: Records demonstrating comparison of actual access with the approved minimum-privilege lists.

requirements.source_text: 2-1-1-2Prohibiting the sharing of approved lists of privileges with unauthorized persons.
requirements.source_summary: Approved privilege lists must not be shared with unauthorized persons.

todo.name: Protect approved privilege lists from unauthorized disclosure
todo.description: Restrict access to approved privilege lists to authorized personnel and apply handling controls that prevent unauthorized viewing, copying, or distribution.

policies.name: Sensitive Access Information Handling Policy
policies.description: Define authorized handling, storage, transmission, and disclosure requirements for approved privilege lists.

policies.name: Information Classification and Access Policy
policies.description: Set access restrictions and protection requirements for records containing privilege information.

documents.name: Privilege List Access Register
documents.description: Record authorized users and approved access to the privilege-list repository.

documents.name: Privilege List Handling Procedure
documents.description: Describe how privilege lists are stored, accessed, transmitted, updated, and securely disposed of.

evidence.name: Repository access logs
evidence.description: Logs showing access to approved privilege lists and identifying users or administrative actions.

evidence.name: Access control configuration
evidence.description: Configuration or permission reports demonstrating that unauthorized personnel cannot access the lists.

evidence.name: Approved handling acknowledgements
evidence.description: Records showing that authorized personnel received and acknowledged applicable handling instructions.

requirements.source_text: 2-1-2Managing identities and access rights to view data using Privileged Access Management systems.
requirements.source_summary: Identities and access rights for viewing data must be managed using Privileged Access Management systems.

todo.name: Manage data-viewing privileges through PAM
todo.description: Configure and operate a Privileged Access Management system to manage identities and data-viewing rights, including controlled privileged access and traceable administration.

policies.name: Privileged Access Management Policy
policies.description: Define the use of PAM for managing privileged identities and access rights to view data.

policies.name: Identity and Access Management Policy
policies.description: Establish requirements for identity lifecycle management, access authorization, and removal of access.

documents.name: PAM Configuration and Administration Standard
documents.description: Specify the PAM architecture, managed accounts, approval settings, session controls, and administrative responsibilities.

documents.name: Privileged Account Inventory
documents.description: Maintain an inventory of privileged identities, associated systems, owners, and approved access.

evidence.name: PAM access and session logs
evidence.description: Logs demonstrating that privileged data-viewing access was brokered or recorded through the PAM system.

evidence.name: PAM configuration reports
evidence.description: System reports showing managed identities, access policies, approvals, and assigned rights.

evidence.name: Privileged account review records
evidence.description: Periodic review records confirming that privileged identities and rights remain authorized.

requirements.source_text: 2-1-3In addition to ECC subcontrol 2-2-3-5,the approved lists of privilegesand privileges used to handle data must be reviewedas specified for each data classification level.At least annuallyAt least every 3 months
requirements.source_summary: Approved privilege lists and privileges used to handle data must be reviewed at the interval specified for the relevant data classification, including the source’s annual and three-month review intervals.

todo.name: Review data privileges at classification-based intervals
todo.description: Perform and document reviews of approved privilege lists and data-handling privileges at the applicable classification-based frequency, including the required annual or three-month interval.

policies.name: Data Privilege Review Policy
policies.description: Define review scope, responsible reviewers, classification-based frequencies, approval requirements, and removal or correction of inappropriate privileges.

documents.name: Privilege Review Schedule
documents.description: Map data classifications to required review intervals and identify responsible reviewers and due dates.

documents.name: Privilege Review Record
documents.description: Document reviewed accounts and privileges, decisions, exceptions, and resulting changes.

evidence.name: Completed privilege review records
evidence.description: Evidence showing that approved lists and data-handling privileges were reviewed at the applicable intervals.

evidence.name: Access change and revocation records
evidence.description: Tickets or system logs showing correction or removal of privileges identified as unnecessary or inappropriate.

evidence.name: Current approved privilege lists
evidence.description: Lists demonstrating that review outcomes were incorporated and appropriately approved.

requirements.source_text: 2-2-1-1Applying security patches and updates from the time of announcement onsystems used to handle data as specified for each data classification level.At least everymonthImmediately
requirements.source_summary: Security patches and updates must be applied to systems used to handle data from the time of announcement, according to the interval specified for each data classification, including the source’s monthly and immediate requirements.

todo.name: Apply security patches and updates within required intervals
todo.description: Monitor patch announcements, assess affected systems used to handle data, and deploy applicable security patches and updates within the interval required for their data classification.

policies.name: Security Patch and Update Management Policy
policies.description: Define patch intake, risk and classification assessment, testing where appropriate, deployment, exception handling, and verification.

documents.name: Patch Management Procedure
documents.description: Describe how announcements are monitored, affected systems identified, patches deployed, and exceptions documented.

documents.name: Data-Handling System Inventory
documents.description: Identify systems used to handle data, their data classifications, owners, and patch-management status.

documents.name: Patch Exception Register
documents.description: Record approved delays or exceptions, their rationale, compensating measures, and remediation dates.

evidence.name: Patch deployment reports
evidence.description: System or management-tool reports showing patch release and installation dates for in-scope systems.

evidence.name: Patch compliance dashboard
evidence.description: Evidence comparing required patch intervals with actual deployment status by data classification.

evidence.name: Patch announcement and assessment records
evidence.description: Records showing receipt of security announcements, affected-system assessment, and deployment decisions.

requirements.source_text: 3-1-1-1Screening orvetting third-party employees who have access to the data.
requirements.source_summary: Third-party employees who have access to the data must be screened or vetted.

todo.name: Screen third-party personnel before granting data access
todo.description: Define and complete appropriate screening or vetting for third-party employees who require data access, and retain the results and access-approval linkage.

policies.name: Third-Party Personnel Screening Policy
policies.description: Define screening or vetting requirements, responsibilities, approval conditions, and handling of screening results for third-party employees with data access.

policies.name: Third-Party Access Management Policy
policies.description: Require verification of personnel authorization before granting, maintaining, or removing third-party data access.

documents.name: Third-Party Personnel Screening Procedure
documents.description: Describe screening initiation, required checks, review of results, exceptions, confidentiality, and record retention.

documents.name: Third-Party Access Register
documents.description: Record third-party employees with data access, sponsoring organization, approved systems or data, and access status.

documents.name: Third-Party Personnel Assurance Records
documents.description: Maintain contractual or supplier records showing applicable screening responsibilities and confirmations.

evidence.name: Completed screening or vetting records
evidence.description: Records demonstrating that third-party employees with data access were screened or vetted.

evidence.name: Third-party access approvals
evidence.description: Approvals linking screened personnel to their authorized data access.

evidence.name: Third-party access register and revocation records
evidence.description: Current and historical records showing who had access and that access was removed when no longer authorized.

requirements.source_text: 3-1-1-2Requiring contractual commitment by third-partiesto securely dispose the organization’s data at the end of the contract or in case of contract termination, including providing evidences of such disposal to the organization.
requirements.source_summary: Third parties must be contractually committed to securely dispose of the organization’s data when the contract ends or is terminated, and to provide the organization with evidence that the disposal occurred.

todo.name: Implement contractual third-party data disposal requirements
todo.description: Review and update applicable third-party contracts to require secure disposal of organizational data at contract completion or termination, including submission of disposal evidence.

policies.name: Third-Party Data Protection Policy
policies.description: Define requirements for protecting and securely disposing of organizational data handled by third parties, including contractual obligations at the end of the relationship.

policies.name: Data Retention and Secure Disposal Policy
policies.description: Establish organizational expectations for data retention, approved disposal methods, and verification of disposal by third parties.

documents.name: Third-Party Contractual Data Disposal Clause
documents.description: Standard contract language requiring secure disposal of organizational data at contract completion or termination and delivery of disposal evidence.

documents.name: Third-Party Data Disposal Register
documents.description: Record third-party data disposal activities, contract or service details, disposal dates, responsible parties, and evidence received.

evidence.name: Executed Third-Party Contracts
evidence.description: Contracts or amendments containing the required secure-disposal and evidence-provision commitments.

evidence.name: Third-Party Disposal Certificates or Attestations
evidence.description: Disposal certificates, signed attestations, destruction logs, or comparable evidence provided by third parties.

evidence.name: Contract Termination Disposal Review Records
evidence.description: Records showing that disposal evidence was requested and reviewed when relevant contracts ended or were terminated.

requirements.source_text: 3-1-1-3Documentingall data sharing operations within third-parties, including data sharing justification.
requirements.source_summary: All data-sharing operations with third parties must be documented, including the justification for sharing the data.

todo.name: Record and justify third-party data-sharing activities
todo.description: Establish and maintain a register of data-sharing operations with third parties, recording the data shared, recipient, purpose, and justification for each operation.

policies.name: Third-Party Data Sharing Policy
policies.description: Set requirements for documenting data shared with third parties and recording the business or operational justification for each sharing activity.

policies.name: Data Governance Policy
policies.description: Define accountability and recordkeeping expectations for data disclosures and exchanges involving external parties.

documents.name: Third-Party Data-Sharing Register
documents.description: Central record of third-party data-sharing operations, including the data involved, recipient, purpose, justification, and relevant agreement or approval references.

documents.name: Data-Sharing Assessment Form
documents.description: Form used to capture and review the purpose, scope, justification, and participating parties for a proposed data-sharing operation.

evidence.name: Completed Data-Sharing Register Entries
evidence.description: Current register records showing third-party data-sharing activities and their documented justifications.

evidence.name: Approved Data-Sharing Assessments
evidence.description: Completed assessments or review records supporting the purpose and justification of selected sharing operations.

evidence.name: Data-Sharing Agreements
evidence.description: Relevant agreements, statements of work, or other records identifying the parties and scope of the data sharing.

requirements.source_text: 3-1-1-4When transferring data outside the kingdom, the capability of the hosting organization abroad to safeguard data must be verified, approval ofthe Authorizing Officialmust be obtained and complyingwith related laws and regulations.
requirements.source_summary: Before transferring data outside the kingdom, the organization must verify that the foreign hosting organization can safeguard the data, obtain approval from the Authorizing Official, and comply with applicable laws and regulations.

todo.name: Approve and assess cross-border data transfers
todo.description: Create a documented review process for transfers outside the kingdom that assesses the foreign hosting organization’s data-safeguarding capability, obtains Authorizing Official approval, and records applicable legal and regulatory compliance.

policies.name: Cross-Border Data Transfer Policy
policies.description: Define the conditions and review steps for transferring data outside the kingdom, including hosting-organization assessment, Authorizing Official approval, and legal compliance.

policies.name: Third-Party Security Assessment Policy
policies.description: Establish requirements for evaluating the capability of foreign hosting organizations to safeguard organizational data before transfer.

documents.name: Cross-Border Data Transfer Assessment
documents.description: Assessment record documenting the destination, hosting organization, data involved, safeguarding capabilities, applicable laws and regulations, and review outcome.

documents.name: Authorizing Official Approval Record
documents.description: Documented approval from the Authorizing Official for the relevant transfer outside the kingdom.

documents.name: Cross-Border Transfer Register
documents.description: Inventory of approved transfers outside the kingdom, including destinations, hosting organizations, data categories, assessment references, and approval status.

evidence.name: Foreign Hosting Organization Security Assessment
evidence.description: Completed due-diligence materials, certifications, questionnaires, or assessment reports supporting the hosting organization’s capability to safeguard the data.

evidence.name: Authorizing Official Approval
evidence.description: Signed or otherwise traceable approval record for the applicable cross-border transfer.

evidence.name: Legal and Regulatory Compliance Review
evidence.description: Documented analysis or review showing consideration of the laws and regulations relevant to the transfer.

evidence.name: Approved Transfer Register Entry
evidence.description: Register entry linking the transfer to its assessment, approval, destination, and data scope.

requirements.source_text: 3-1-1-5Requiring third-parties to notify the organization immediately in case of cybersecurity incident that may affect data that has been shared or created.
requirements.source_summary: Third parties must notify the organization immediately when a cybersecurity incident may affect data that has been shared with or created by the third party.

todo.name: Require immediate third-party incident notification
todo.description: Add and monitor contractual requirements for third parties to immediately notify the organization of cybersecurity incidents that may affect shared or third-party-created organizational data.

policies.name: Third-Party Cybersecurity Incident Management Policy
policies.description: Define third-party notification expectations, escalation responsibilities, and handling requirements for incidents affecting shared or created data.

policies.name: Supplier Security Policy
policies.description: Establish security obligations for suppliers and service providers, including prompt communication of relevant cybersecurity incidents.

documents.name: Third-Party Incident Notification Clause
documents.description: Standard contractual clause requiring immediate notification of cybersecurity incidents that may affect shared or third-party-created data.

documents.name: Third-Party Incident Notification Procedure
documents.description: Procedure for receiving, escalating, assessing, and responding to incident notifications from third parties.

documents.name: Third-Party Incident Log
documents.description: Record of third-party incident notifications, affected data, notification timing, actions taken, and closure status.

evidence.name: Executed Third-Party Agreements
evidence.description: Contracts or service agreements containing the immediate cybersecurity incident notification requirement.

evidence.name: Third-Party Incident Notifications
evidence.description: Incident reports, emails, tickets, or other records demonstrating notifications received from third parties where applicable.

evidence.name: Incident Response and Escalation Records
evidence.description: Records showing that third-party notifications were logged, assessed, escalated, and handled by the organization.

requirements.source_text: 3-1-1-6Reclassifying data to the least level to achieve the objective before sharing it with third-parties using data masking or data scrambling techniques.
requirements.source_summary: Before sharing data with third parties, the organization must reclassify it to the lowest classification level that still achieves the sharing objective, using data masking or data scrambling techniques.

todo.name: Minimize and obfuscate data before third-party sharing
todo.description: Review data proposed for third-party sharing, assign the least classification level that supports the intended objective, and apply suitable masking or scrambling before disclosure.

policies.name: Data Classification and Handling Policy
policies.description: Define classification, reclassification, and handling expectations for data shared with third parties, including use of the least level needed for the objective.

policies.name: Data Masking and Scrambling Policy
policies.description: Establish requirements for selecting and applying masking or scrambling techniques before third-party data sharing.

documents.name: Third-Party Data-Sharing Assessment
documents.description: Record identifying the sharing objective, original and revised data classification, minimum data required, and selected protection technique.

documents.name: Data Masking or Scrambling Standard
documents.description: Technical and procedural standard describing approved methods for masking or scrambling data before external sharing.

documents.name: Data Transformation Record
documents.description: Record of the data set shared, transformation performed, date, responsible personnel, and link to the relevant sharing approval or assessment.

evidence.name: Completed Data Classification Assessments
evidence.description: Records showing that data intended for third-party sharing was evaluated and reclassified to the least level needed for the stated objective.

evidence.name: Masked or Scrambled Data Samples
evidence.description: Representative shared-data samples or controlled demonstrations showing application of masking or scrambling.

evidence.name: Data Transformation Logs
evidence.description: System or process logs documenting the masking or scrambling operation applied before transfer.

evidence.name: Third-Party Sharing Review Records
evidence.description: Review or approval records linking the sharing purpose to the minimized and transformed data set.
